body: Since the beginning of European colonization, the coastal town of Negombo has maintained a prominent Roman Catholic majority, existing alongside communities of Buddhists, Hindus, and Muslims. Successive occupations by the Portuguese, Dutch, and British led to a unique architectural amalgamation of Sri Lankan and European styles. Negombo is widely known as "Little Rome" due to its numerous highly ornate, Portuguese-era Roman Catholic churches. St. Mary’s Church is a prime example, distinguished by its classical columns and stunning painted depictions of Christ on the ceiling. Construction of the church commenced in the latter part of 1874 and was completed after a significantly long gap in 1922. Photo Opportunity: A bench (with Jesus sitting) outside the church provides a peaceful spot for visitors to sit, reflect, and take memorable photographs.
title: Little Rome in Negombo

body: St. Mary's Church in Negombo stands as a testament to the rich cultural and religious heritage of Sri Lanka, offering visitors a glimpse into its history and architectural beauty.St. Mary's Church in Negombo is a significant landmark that beautifully blends colonial architecture with Sri Lankan religious traditions. Located in the heart of Negombo town, this historic church dates back to the 19th century and holds a special place in the local Catholic community.The exterior of St. Mary's Church is striking with its tall spire and Gothic-style architecture, adorned with intricate details and stained glass windows that depict religious scenes. The interior is equally impressive, with a serene atmosphere enhanced by ornate decorations, statues of saints, and a tranquil nave that invites quiet contemplation.Visitors to St. Mary's Church can admire its historical artifacts, including old paintings and statues that reflect the church's long-standing presence in Negombo. The church's peaceful ambiance makes it a perfect place for both prayer and reflection, offering solace amidst its historical significance.Beyond its architectural beauty, St. Mary's Church plays a vital role in the local community, hosting religious ceremonies, festivals, and cultural events throughout the year. These events provide visitors with an opportunity to experience the vibrant spiritual life of Negombo's Catholic community firsthand.The church is conveniently located near other attractions in Negombo, making it easy for visitors to include in their itinerary. Nearby, you'll find local markets, eateries offering traditional Sri Lankan cuisine, and scenic spots like Negombo Beach, perfect for rounding out your visit with additional experiences.In conclusion, St. Mary's Church in Negombo is not only a religious sanctuary but also a historical and cultural gem that offers a glimpse into Sri Lanka's rich heritage. Whether you're interested in architecture, history, or spiritual experiences, a visit to St. Mary's Church promises a memorable and enriching journey through time and faith.
title: Historical Gem in Negombo - St. Mary's Church

Its construction began in 1874 and was completed in 1922. • Architecture: The church features a blend of Gothic and neoclassical architectural styles. Its interior is adorned with beautiful paintings, statues, and intricate ceiling art depicting various religious scenes. • Cultural Importance: Located in Negombo, a city known for its large Christian community, St. Mary’s Church serves as a central place of worship and plays a vital role in the religious life of the local population. • Tourist Attraction: The church is a popular tourist attraction, drawing visitors interested in its architecture, history, and the serene ambiance it provides. Its location in Negombo makes it accessible for those staying in the city or passing through on their way to or from Colombo and the Bandaranaike International Airport. • Events and Services: The church hosts regular masses and special events, particularly during significant Christian holidays such as Christmas and Easter, attracting large congregations.St. Mary’s Church stands as a testament to the rich cultural and religious heritage of Negombo, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring the region.

body: St. Mary’s Church with its gothic columns and clean cream walls, situated in the heart of Negombo town, is the grandest and one of the biggest cathedrals in Sri Lanka. The fading pink chamber has the most awesome thunderous religious painting covering the nave and wonderful alabaster statues of various saints. All across its upper walls outside the aisle, are religious statuettes. N.S. Godamanne, a local Buddhist painter, did the unique paintings on the the life of Christ on the ceiling. Though its construction began in 1874, it was only completed 50 years later - in 1922. Negombo, being predominantly influenced by the Christian faith, is known as ‘Little Rome’ due to its Roman Catholic churches of the Portuguese era. The cost of one of the altars which was imported from Europe was paid for by a testator. Peaceful and quiet ambience. Would recommend a visit
title: Come Pray With Me at St. Mary’s Church!

body: The St. Mary’s Church, Negombo is landmark edifice, a Roman Catholic church in the heart of the Negombo town. Its exterior surface is painted in pink colour. It is one the largest cathedrals in Sri Lanka.The St. Mary’s Church, Negombo is landmark edifice, a Roman Catholic church in the heart of the Negombo town. Its exterior surface is painted in pink colour. It is one the largest cathedrals in Sri Lanka.Negombo has been influenced greatly by the Christian faith from the time it was occupied by the Portuguese. It is often called "Little Rome" in view of the large number of churches in the town.Construction of the church was started in 1874 and completed, after a long gap, in 1922. The art and architecture of this church and a few similar other churches in Sri Lanka demonstrate the cultural amalgamation of the European practice with Sri Lankan art and architecture during the early years of the 20th century.

title: Worth a look

body: Great place to be. There was a ceremony when we visited the church premises. nice building with dutch structures.Large garden area and beautiful arts in side the church.
title: Probably one of the Oldest Churches
Church of Santa Maria (Careful there are more than one) the biggest Roman Catholic Church in the, a must to visit
body: Magnificent wonderfully clean church in a setting of absolute poverty. Local Fishing Communities contributions built and continue to maintain the building and grounds. A true reminder of absolute faith

title: St Marry Church is place to Visit in Negombo,
body: One of the intarasting Church arround in Negombo,Here you will see very good ceiling painted by a local artist.

title: Big church
body: This is a fine building. A holy place that is not after rs for entry. Good for a look around and if there is something going on even better

title: Nice church to visit
body: Spacious church, which can be accessed from all sides. No problem when taking pictures.Just wait with that when for example a mass or funeral is going on.

title: Unfortunately shut
body: A massive neo-Rocoque building near the town centre; it unfortunately seemed to be shut at our visit. The anti-abortion lobby was still active, though...

title: pinky
body: interesting pinky colour of the building.it's a pity we couldn't get inside because it was overcrowded... not with tourist but with the guests of the wedding ceremony which took place at the time we've been there.. catрolic сeremony in sri-lankian way...interesting

title: St Mary's Church
body: A large church which has beautiful religious statues.The ceiling of this church has fresco's and is one of the largest churches in Negombo.

title: Greta Master Peice
body: One of the oldest Churches we were said was St. Mary's Church. Very Nice, nice arts and great place.
